property_summary: After a Collect call with amount _am, the caller's balance decreases by exactly _am if msg.sender.call succeeds, regardless of whether balances[msg.sender] >= MinSum.
Collect always deducts an amount exactly equal to _am from the caller's balance only when both conditions (balance >= MinSum and balance >= _am) hold; otherwise no deduction occurs.
Collect never decreases any address's balance unless both conditions (balance >= _am and balance >= MinSum) held and the transfer succeeded.
Collect will only decrease the caller's balance if both conditions (balance >= MinSum and balance >= _am) held before the call.
For any address k, the balance recorded in C's balances mapping after a Collect call is at least (original balance[k] - _am) when the caller satisfies the conditions; otherwise it remains unchanged.
After a Collect call, the caller's balance never increases.
After Collect, the sum of all balances and contract balance is invariant; the bug causes the total supply to increase.
After Collect, the caller's balance is reduced exactly by the amount withdrawn, never increased.
The sum of all account balances in the mapping plus the contract's own balance is invariant (unchanged) before and after a Collect call.
After any Collect, the caller's balances mapping value is at least the original minus the amount, not plus.
After Collect, the caller's balance is the sum of initial balance, deposits, and withdrawals minus collected amount, invariant under fuzzed sequences
After Collect is called, the total balance sum over all addresses does not decrease compared to before the call.
The balances mapping at any address never exceeds its value if assignment were addition (i.e., deposits never decrease balance).
After Collect is called, the delta in the caller's balance equals the collected amount minus the change in the contract's total ether balance.
After Collect, the balances of any address that never called Deposit or Collect remain unchanged.
After Collect, MinSum equals the value set by SetMinSum, not zero.

After a successful Collect call that does not revert, the MinSum state variable will be unchanged from its value set by SetMinSum (if SetMinSum was called) or will remain at its default zero (if SetMinSum was not called) — in the reference, it is never zeroed by Collect, but in the bug it is always zero regardless.
After a successful Collect call that does not revert, the MinSum state variable remains unchanged from its value set by SetMinSum
After a successful Collect call (no revert), the value of MinSum equals the value last set by SetMinSum, not zero.
After any sequence of calls ending with Collect, the MinSum state variable remains unchanged from its previous value.
After calling Collect with any amount, MinSum remains unchanged.
After a successful collect operation, the value of MinSum is unchanged from its initial value.
After a call to Collect, the value of MinSum equals the value it was set to during initialization when intitalized is true.
After any call to Collect(uint256), the value of MinSum stored in C is equal to 0 (its initial value) when initialized is true.
After any call to Collect, the value of MinSum is unchanged from its previous value, provided the call does not revert due to insufficient balance.
After Collect() call, the total ether in the contract plus that in the caller's balance equals the sum before the call minus _am.
After a successful Collect() call, the sender's balance decreases by exactly _am and the contract's balance decreases by exactly _am.
A Collect call that reverts does not change the caller's balance in the contract's balances mapping.
A Collect call that succeeds (does not revert) increases the ether balance of msg.sender by exactly the requested amount _am.
After Collect() is called, the contract's Log state variable (via its getter) must equal the address that was passed to SetLogFile().
After any sequence of calls leading to a Collect call, the caller's ETH balance increase equals the collected amount when conditions are met.

After a collect call that succeeds (reverts in buggy version but not in reference), the buggy version's Deposit function is never called (its msg.value is not added to balances), so the invariant that the sum of all balances and the contract's ETH balance equals total deposits is broken.
After a successful Collect call (no revert), the contract's ETH balance decreases exactly by the collected amount.

After any sequence of calls ending with a successful Collect, the caller's balance in the contract is unchanged or decreases exactly by the collected amount, and the contract's ETH balance decreases by the same amount.

After any Collect call, the caller's balance in the contract is always less than or equal to its value before the call, and the contract's ETH balance decreases exactly by the collected amount when the call succeeds.
After a Collect call, the caller's balance decreases exactly by the amount withdrawn, and the contract's ether balance decreases by the same amount.
After Collect(uint256) reverts, the caller's balance in the contract remains unchanged.
After Collect(uint256) reverts, the caller's ether balance remains unchanged.
After Collect(uint256), the caller's balance in the contract is always less than the caller's balance before the call plus the MinSum threshold.
After Collect(uint256), the caller's balance in the contract is reduced by exactly the withdrawn amount only if the original MinSum condition was met; otherwise the call reverts.
The balance of the caller never increases after a successful Collect call.
After a successful Collect call, the balance of msg.sender in the contract decreases by exactly _am.
The sum of all balances in the contract never increases after a Collect call.

After a Collect call reverses subtraction to addition, the invariant that the sender's balance never increases as a result of Collect is correct; instead add a precondition to ensure the reference always passes.
After a successful Collect call, the total balance of the contract decreases by exactly _am.
For any address and any amount, calling Collect with amount zero must not revert.
When Collect is called with amount zero on an initialized contract, it must revert for any address.
Calling Collect with amount zero results in a revert in the buggy version but not in the reference version.
When Collect is called with a non-negative amount, if the sender's balance is less than MinSum or less than the amount, the call must not revert.
When Collect is called with a non-negative amount on an initialized contract, the call must not revert solely due to the amount being zero whereas the reference allows a successful no-op.
